chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'a from someone else from Aban ibn Uthman from Misma'a from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said:
My father used to view for these two Harams what he did not view for other than these two, and he was saying: 'The completion (of prayer) in them is from the matters of the preserved treasures'.

key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two Harams (sanctuaries), referring to Masjid al-Haram in Mecca and Masjid al-Nabi in Medina
key_terms.الْمَذْخُورِ: Preserved/Storehouse (referring to divine treasures or special merits)

ai.seo_question: What is the special ruling regarding prayer completion in the two Harams according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) narrates that his father, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), emphasized the superior merit of performing complete prayers (al-itmam) within the two Harams of Mecca and Medina. This practice is described as part of 'al-amr al-madhkhor' (the preserved/accumulated reward), highlighting the unique spiritual gravity and jurisprudential status of these sanctuaries in Shia tradition. The narration underscores the belief that acts of worship performed in these specific locations carry multiplied and distinct divine blessings.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad,f rom Ibn Sama’at, from someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Misma’a, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said:

‘Myasws fatherasws used to view for these two Harrams what heasws did not view for other than these two, and heasws was saying: ‘The complete (Salaat) in these two is from the matters of the preserved treasures’.
en.sarwar: 7. Humayd ibn Ziyad from ibn Sama‘ah from more than one person from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from Misma’ who has said the following: “Abu Ibrahim, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

My father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would see for these two al- Haram (the sacred area) what he would not see for other places and say that performing Salat (prayer) therein in complete form is of the saving matters.’”
